newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks end slightly up, thirdliners active.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks end slightly up, thirdliners active.

text.p: Manila shares closed up on Monday after the index traded in a narrow range for most of the session as the focus was on secondary and tertiary stocks, traders said.

"The market was very bullish on second and thirdliners but most blue chips remained steady, an indication that foreign fund managers have yet to show their presence," said Ike Wee, assistant vice-president at Lippo Securities.
The index ended 4.18 points up, or 0.12 percent, at 3,386.02.

"We saw a lot of action on companies owned by businessman Alfredo Ramos as punters fed on rumours that these firms will be converted into holding companies," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities Inc.

These companies include oil exploration firm Philodrill Corp which closed up 0.25 centavos, or 26.32 percent, at 1.20 centavos; and gold miner United Paragon Mining Co which rose 1.30 centavos, or 41.67 percent, to 1.70 centavos.
Of the blue chips, only Manila Electric Corp B closed up in heavy volume, gaining three pesos to 229.00 pesos.
There were 62 gainers compared to 61 decliners with 77 issues unchanged. Value turnover was 2.5 billion pesos.
Traders said the market's value turnover will likely pick up by midweek as the market would have recovered from the effects of the Chinese lunar new year holidays.
"We are still in a consolidation phase and the index will likely move sideways for the early part of the week," said Garcia.
